text: Oh brilliant, the flight's delayed four hours. Love airports. Love this plastic chair. Love the eleven-euro sandwich.
Wonderful, Simon 'forgot' to book the venue. Very cool of him, two days before the party.
Yay, another Monday. My favourite thing.
Sure, I'd love to redo the whole report because the client changed their mind about the font.
Great start to the holiday: food poisoning on night one. Living the dream.
I'm not even angry anymore about the lie. Just disappointed and quiet.
For once I'm not anxious before the flight. Slept fine. Packed calmly.
Didn't feel lonely at all this weekend, which surprised me. Busy with the garden and the neighbours popped round.
I wouldn't say I'm happy about the move. But I'm not dreading it anymore either. Somewhere in the middle.
No regrets about leaving. None. Okay, maybe one, about the people.
Not grateful for the 'feedback' Darren gave me in front of everyone. Not at all.
I'm not tired, I'm just done with this week. Is that different? It feels different.
Apple announced the new phone and Jack immediately ordered two. Meanwhile Amazon still hasn't delivered my kettle.
Lunch with Rose at the Rose and Crown. She ordered the rosé, obviously.
Hope visited today. My cousin Hope, not the feeling. Though both, honestly.
Walked Max and Bella in the rain. Both dogs soaked and delighted. Me, less so.
Bumped into 'Big Dave' from the old job. Still calls me 'Professor'. Still owes me a tenner.
Dr. Who marathon with Tomoko. Ten episodes. No regrets.
Netflix raised the price again. Cancelled it. Spotify next probably.
June was hard. July is better. Grace, my therapist, says that's what healing looks like: uneven.
Called Mum, then Ma Li from next door, then Mr. B at the shop about the parcel. Social day.
Paris with Florence. Florence hated Paris. I loved it. We argued in front of the Louvre.
Got the results: distinction. Wanted to call Grandpa first like always. Then remembered. Sat on the stairs holding the letter.
Engaged! Over the moon. Also terrified about telling Dad, who has opinions about Javi.
Leaving the job I've had for nine years. Relief, grief, excitement, guilt, all in one cardboard box.
Glad the surgery's over, scared of what the biopsy will say.
Proud of Amina for leaving. Sad she's gone. Both true.
Happy for Lars getting the promotion, a bit jealous if I'm honest, mostly happy.
Bittersweet day. Last chemo session. Rang the bell. Thought of everyone in the ward who never got to.
I keep laughing at Ollie's jokes on the phone and then crying after I hang up. Long distance is weird.
Last week I would have panicked about this deadline. This week I'm getting on with it.
Two years ago today I was in the hospital. Today I ran up the hill behind the house.
Tomorrow is Mum's anniversary. I'm dreading the day and also want to mark it properly.
Next Friday I'll know about the job. Until then, normal life, apparently.
By 2030 I want to have my own studio. Wrote it down today so it's real.
Funny how my chest unclenched the moment the plane touched down at home.
I keep reorganising the spice rack instead of opening the letter from the court.
Made his favourite dinner and set two plates before I remembered.
Hummed the whole way to work. People looked at me. Didn't care.
Checked the baby monitor nine times between 11 and midnight.
Ate the whole cake standing over the sink at 1am. Again. Third night this week.
Kept the voicemail. Listen to it most nights before sleep.
Bought a second toothbrush for the bathroom. Rina's staying over more and more.
Lights off at 9. Can't remember the last time I made it to the end of a film.
Fine.
Meh.
Ugh.
Best day ever!!!
Can't.

Today was the day I finally went back to the climbing wall after the fall. I'd been avoiding it for four months, telling myself I was busy, telling Sol I'd lost interest, telling myself the wrist still hurt when it really didn't. I stood at the bottom of the easiest route for a long time. My hands were sweating so much I had to chalk them three times. The first few moves were fine. Then at the point where I fell last time I froze, and the old panic came up my throat. I breathed. I looked at my feet. I made the move. I got to the top of a route a child could climb and I sat at the top crying a bit. Sol was below grinning. I'm so proud of myself I could burst.

Long one today because I need to get it out. The meeting with the department head was supposed to be about my workload. Instead she spent forty minutes explaining why the restructure was 'an opportunity' and then, at the very end, mentioned that my role 'won't exist in its current form' from January. Not that I'm losing my job, exactly, just that I'll have to reapply for one of the new roles, alongside Amit and Clare and probably half the floor. I nodded and asked sensible questions and thanked her for her time, because apparently that's who I am. Then I went to the stairwell and shook. I have a mortgage. I have Theo's nursery fees. I've been here eleven years. I don't even know what I'd write on an application. I keep imagining the interview panel looking at me and seeing someone who stopped growing years ago. I couldn't eat dinner.

Sunday, and the whole family came for lunch for the first time since Nonna's funeral. I was worried it would be sad, that we'd all sit around her empty chair and not know what to say. Instead Zio Franco told the story about Nonna chasing the priest out of the kitchen with a wooden spoon, and everyone laughed until they cried, and then just cried, and then laughed again. My niece Bianca made the gnocchi using Nonna's recipe and they were lumpy and perfect. We stayed at the table until it was dark. Nobody wanted to clear the plates. Driving home I felt full in every sense, grateful that we still have each other and still have her, in the stories and the recipes and the noise.

I want to write down how the day actually went because I keep telling people 'fine'. Woke up at five with the baby. Fed her, changed her, she was sick on both of us, changed us both. Kwesi left at seven for his shift. By nine I'd had half a coffee and no breakfast. The health visitor came at eleven and I'd forgotten, so she found me in yesterday's T-shirt surrounded by washing. She was kind about it. In the afternoon the baby cried for two hours straight and I cried with her for some of it. I love her so much it scares me and I'm so tired I can feel my heartbeat in my eyes. Kwesi got home at eight and took her and I fell asleep sitting up on the sofa. That's the day. Not fine. But we're alive and fed and that's something.

Spent most of today going back over the year and I don't think I've done that honestly before. In January I was sure the move would fix everything: new city, new job, new me. It didn't, of course. The loneliness came with me in the suitcase. By spring I was eating dinner in front of the laptop every night and telling Nell on the phone that I was 'really settling in'. Something turned around in summer when I joined the running club on a whim. Not because running is magic but because three mornings a week people expected me to show up. I made two friends. I started saying yes. I'm not sure what lesson to take from it all. Maybe that places don't change you, but small routines with other people in them do. I want to remember that.

I'm writing this on the train back from the hospital and I'm so angry I can barely hold the pen. They discharged Dad yesterday even though he could hardly stand, because they 'needed the bed'. No care plan, no follow-up, a bag of pills and a leaflet. Last night he fell in the bathroom and lay there for two hours before the neighbour heard him. Now he's back in A&E with a fractured hip and the same doctor who discharged him is acting like it's bad luck. It isn't bad luck. It's a system that treats old people like parcels. I made a formal complaint and the woman at the desk sighed at me like I was the problem. I wanted to scream at someone and there was nobody to scream at who deserved it.

Long walk with Zeynep along the cliffs. We set out meaning to talk about her wedding plans and ended up talking about everything else: our mothers, her doubts about her job, my doubts about everything, the way the sea looks different every single time. At one point we sat on a bench with a plaque for someone who 'loved this view' and didn't say anything for a while. Then a gull stole her sandwich and we laughed so hard a passing couple stopped to ask if we were okay. I came home sunburnt and windswept and lighter than I've felt in months. There's nothing like a friend who has known you for twenty years and still wants to hear what you think.

I'm trying to work out why I feel so flat when on paper the week went well. I finished the project. The client was pleased. Hamid and I had a nice dinner on Thursday. My mum's test results were normal. And still, all week, I've had this grey feeling sitting on my chest, like I'm watching my own life through a window. I don't think it's sadness exactly, more like nothing reaches me. I slept badly most nights. I didn't go to the gym. I've cancelled plans with friends twice. I noticed today that I haven't listened to music in weeks, and music is usually the first thing I reach for. Writing it down makes it look more serious than it felt. Maybe I should mention it to someone.

Opening night. I've been in rehearsals for eight weeks and today it all came together. The set wobbled during the second act, Ruairi forgot a whole page and I had to improvise us back into the scene, and the lights went out for three seconds in the finale. None of it mattered. The audience laughed in all the right places and in a few wrong ones that were even better. When we took the bow I could see Mum in the third row clapping with her hands above her head like she does. Afterwards in the dressing room everyone was hugging and shouting and someone opened cheap prosecco. My face hurts from smiling. I want to do this for the rest of my life.

Today I told my parents I'm not going to do the law degree. I'd planned the conversation for weeks. I chose the moment carefully, after dinner, after Dad's second cup of tea. I explained about the design course, the portfolio, the scholarship I've already applied for. Mum went very quiet. Dad said 'we'll talk about it later' and turned on the television. That was it. No shouting, which I'd prepared for, but no support either. I'm sitting in my room now feeling sick and stubborn in equal measure. I know I'm right. I know it's my life. I just wish knowing you're right felt better than this. I don't know if they'll come round. I'm going to go anyway.

It's three in the morning and the house is silent and I feel calm in a way I haven't for months. The decision is made. I'm leaving the band. We talked it through tonight, all four of us, around the kitchen table at Ines's place, and it was sad and honest and nobody was cruel. They understand. I'll still help with the album, I'll play the last gig in December, and after that I'm going to try being someone who has weekends. I thought I'd feel panic or grief. Instead there's this long exhale. I've been carrying the guilt of wanting out for a year. Now it's said out loud, and the world didn't end. I'm going to sleep well tonight.
Exam results day. I got a B in chemistry, which I'm thrilled about after failing the mocks.
Results came out: B in chem! After failing the mocks I honestly thought I'd get a D. So happy.
Missed the bus again because the timetable changed and nobody told us. Late for work, again.
Bus timetable changed with no notice. Missed it. Late to work for the second time this week.
Nadia called to say the biopsy was benign. I've been holding my breath for two weeks.
Benign! Nadia rang this afternoon with the results. Two weeks of waiting and it's nothing.
First night alone in the new house. Every creak sounds like a person. Lights on in every room.
New house, first night on my own. Jumping at every noise. I've left all the lights on.
Grandma taught me her bread recipe today. My hands, her hands, the same dough.
Baked bread with Grandma. She showed me how she kneads it. Felt like being handed something precious.
Thinking about calling Ewan. Then not calling him. Then thinking about it again.
I don't know what I feel about the news. Maybe nothing yet. Maybe it'll hit tomorrow.
A strange, floaty day. Like being in between two versions of myself.
Everyone keeps saying congratulations and I keep saying thank you and it doesn't feel like it's happening to me.
I can't tell if I'm sad about the move or just tired from packing.
Today I said 'love you' to Ifeanyi by accident at the end of a work call. He said 'love you too' and then we both hung up very fast.
Is it bad that I feel relieved Grandad isn't suffering anymore? I'm sad. I'm also relieved.
Woke up with a weird mix of dread and excitement about the first day. Mostly dread.
Lucy and Lucía both came to the party and I kept calling them by each other's names. Mortifying. Fun though.
Message from 'Unknown Number': 'Is this Sam?' It is not Sam. I am not Sam. Nobody here is Sam.
Mrs. Kaur's grandson, the one who plays violin, gave a concert in the community hall. Mrs. Kaur glowed all evening.
Tried the new place, Mama Rosa's. Pizza was average. Service was slow. Won't go back.
Sat with Sergeant Okoye at the veterans' lunch. He told me about the war like it was yesterday.
Saw 'The Fall of Rome' at the theatre with Gwen. Three hours. Gwen slept for one of them.
Called my old teacher, Mr. Abara, to say I'm finally a teacher too. He said 'took you long enough' and laughed.
Pfft. The 'mandatory fun' team-building day. Trust falls and soggy sandwiches.
Absolutely thrilled to be spending my birthday at the tax office. Truly.
Oh good, the cat was sick on my laptop. Productivity unlocked.
What a joy, a 6am fire alarm drill in December. Everyone in pyjamas in the snow.
So I'm not invited to the wedding. Fine. Totally fine. Definitely not hurt.
Haven't cried once since the funeral. People seem to expect it. I just feel numb.
I don't miss him. I don't. I just keep checking whether he's posted anything.
Never been less excited about a holiday. Need it, don't want it.
Not proud of how I spoke to Ade today. Need to apologise tomorrow.
No worries about the presentation this time. I know the material cold.
Gratitude isn't coming easily today. Everything feels heavy and I can't find the bright side.
There's no anger left, only tiredness. Two years of fighting with the council will do that.
Spent the afternoon at the cemetery tidying Mum's grave. Planted primroses. Talked to her for a while about the kids. It was peaceful, not sad.
Wasn't expecting much from the blind date. Turns out Kofi is hilarious and we talked until the café closed.
I'm not okay, but I'm going to be. That's the honest version.
